text:
ravi: Alerting: brief spike of GPU attach errors in ap-southeast1 beginning ~01:47 UTC. root cause looks like janitor warmup + rewrite waves saturating per-host NVMe IOPS, causing attach timeouts.
sam: any sample logs?
ravi: from gnode-apse1-210:
```
[  107.432100] nvme0n1: write timeout, aborting command
[  107.432250] writeback: I/O error, dev nvme0n1
[  107.432480] provisioner: failed to allocate scratch (timeout)
```
maria: we increased janitor_warmup_threads to 16 yesterday to speed reclaim. that could explain large concurrent write bursts.
toni: blast radius: ~20% attach failures for ~7m in the regional gpu pool, most recovered via fallback but start latencies jump. no external customer errors yet.
sam: quick mitigation: set janitor_warmup_threads=4 on a 5-host canary and apply a per-host soft iops ceiling of 50k wkB/s. also add a temporary routing rule to prefer eu-west for new batch allocs.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026 created: "ap-southeast1 nvme iops wave => gpu attach timeouts" (severity: medium)
maria: recommend we also add a yield check in janitor to back off when nvme util > 80%. I'll open a small PR.
ravi: canary flipped; nvme util dropped within 90s and attach success rate returned to normal. expanding rollout in 10m. :thumbsup:
